We have studied a group of 11 post-starburst galaxies and 3 dormant Balmer-strong galaxies with the Hubble Space Telescope in their centers, finding a diverse range of transient events. These transients include 7 supernovae, 3 tidal disruptions, and 1 transient similar to ASASSN-15l. By comparing the colors and brightness of these transients to known supernovae and tidal disruptions, we were able to determine their likely nature in 9 cases, with 2 remaining transients possibly being supernovae or tidal disruptions. Our findings suggest that post-starburst galaxies are often associated with tidal disruptions, while transient events in dormant Balmer-strong galaxies appear to be less common than in post-starburst galaxies. This could indicate that these galaxies contain large amounts of dark matter, causing their cores to be more massive than average.

In reconfigurable wireless networks, the scheduler plays a vital role in controlling the QoS by allocating resources to each application. The scheduler's performance significantly impacts the overall QoS experience. This paper presents a novel performer-critic learning-based QoS-conscious scheduler called PC-lQoS, designed to optimize scheduling and performance. The scheduler consists of a performer and a critic that are trained together using a multi-step reinforcement learning approach. The performer is a Mixture of Experts model, and the critic is a performer that utilizes expert output and a linear combination of past states. The proposed approach enables the model to adapt to QoS variations and learn from past experiences. The simulations demonstrate that PC-lQoS outperforms PC-MERES and baseline algorithms in terms of QoS efficiency.

The visual appeal of text can significantly impact a reader's desire to continue reading content. To improve the aesthetic quality of text, researchers have developed automated post-editing tools that refine text for human consumption. Assessing the overall visual appeal of text is still an ongoing challenge, so we propose a new approach using word-level evaluations. We tested this method against existing post-editing tasks, finding that our word-level assessments yield more accurate ratings. To measure the impact of our word-level evaluations, we incorporated a reward system that penalizes subjects for poor post-editing outcomes. Our results show that the proposed enhancement leads to noticeable improvements in text quality and reduces the need for post-editing corrections.

We investigate how the information from black hole silhouettes can be utilized to calculate the value of the cosmological constant, $\Lambda$, and demonstrate that a certain condition is required for this. By establishing a basic equation that relates the observed ratio of the photon sphere area to the black hole mass to the cosmological constant, we determine a condition that allows this information to be effectively used. Additionally, we derive a more advanced expression that links the photon sphere area ratio to the event horizon area and show that this relationship can be used to calculate the value of $\Lambda$ in cases where the above condition is satisfied.

A novel approach has been developed for solving the relativistic shockwave equations across two-dimensional Cartesian coordinates, offering a more comprehensive framework than the established Einfeldt method. The new formulation achieves comparable accuracy in simulating shock waves, shock interactions, and expansion processes while enhancing computational efficiency. The improved method boasts increased simplicity, versatility, speed, and flexibility, enabling a single set of equations to represent diverse relativistic hydrodynamic phenomena. Leveraging a unique characteristic variable enables the reduction of the two-dimensional time-evolution equation to a single hyperbolic partial differential equation. The novel formulation exhibits similar numerical stability and accuracy as its Einfeldt counterpart, with the added benefit of processing expansion equations using the same framework, eliminating the need for separate numerical methods.

An analysis of B plus meson decays into D plus K zero meson and D plus K plus meson final states, using a dataset of 3 inverse femtobarns collected by the LHCb experiment, is presented. D star plus K zero D star zero K plus, D star plus K zero D star zero K plus decay modes, corresponding to the decay of one D star plus meson and a K minus K plus Cabibbo-suppressed D star plus meson, are observed for the first time.

This study aims to delve into the properties of fractal polynomials on the Sierpiński gasket and explore the compact sets that admit fractal bases. The gasket's distinct nature allows for a more in-depth examination of these polynomials than in traditional settings, leading to intriguing observations. The ultimate goal is to provide a comprehensive description of the compact sets in the S-shaped domain, focusing on the fractal sets that shape the gasket's geometry and serve as its structural foundation.

Visual information drives human understanding and knowledge acquisition.
Visual inquiries, such as questions that involve observation, play a vital role
in directing attention towards specific details. We introduce a method to create
visual questions based on a given image and an existing question, where the
generated question has a distinct answer but differs from the original one.
This approach can be adapted to produce multiple new questions for a set of
given images, maintaining the diversity and variety of the resulting questions.
We demonstrate the effectiveness of our method through both automated and
human evaluations, showcasing its ability to generate a more targeted and
informative set of questions for a given image.

We examine the hypothesis that core-cusp density profiles in haloes are transformed to core-halo profiles through a two-stage process, driven by supernova (SN) feedback in isolated, dark matter-free galaxies. The first stage, core-cusp reversal, is triggered by SN feedback in galaxies with relatively low masses and is facilitated by SN feedback in the outer regions of these galaxies. The second stage, core dissolution, is initiated when the total SN energy deposited within the central region of galaxies exceeds its binding energy. The second stage is characterized by SN feedback in the central regions of these galaxies. Building on the work of Jacobson, Schuster and Natarajan, who previously proposed this two-stage process, we use N-body simulations to test this hypothesis. The results of our simulations indicate that core-cusp haloes are converted to core-density profiles in the inner regions, with central densities increasing by a factor of up to 5. The results also show that this conversion is achieved within a Gyr timescale, which is consistent with the cosmic age at redshift $z=6$. The results also indicate that the core-cusp haloes are converted to core-density profiles in the inner regions, with central densities increasing by a factor of up to 20. For the past twenty years, advancements in resolution elimination have led to impressive improvements in SAT solving. Our comprehensive study delves into the relationship between resolution and move elimination, identifying a unified approach that encompasses both methods. The study also introduces the concept of weighted move elimination as a refinement of these techniques, enabling the development of efficient algorithms that outperform existing resolution and topological move elimination methods.

This study focuses on replicator equations with n dimensions that have a specific type of dynamics where the power function is continuous and non-negative, and specifically examines the dynamics where the power function is continuous and non-negative, and is often referred to as "similar-order preserving". The research shows that in this particular case, the dynamics exhibits either a specific type of behavior known as "washout" or a specific type of behavior known as "expanding", and in certain cases, the system can achieve a specific type of behavior known as "expanding fixed points". Additionally, the study shows that in systems with two dimensions that have a specific type of dynamics where the power function is continuous and non-negative, the system can achieve a specific type of behavior known as "specific type of behavior known as "steady state" or a specific type of behavior known as "expanding fixed points". The research also shows that in systems with more than two dimensions that have a specific type of dynamics where the power function is continuous and non-negative, the system can achieve a specific type of behavior known as either "steady state" or a specific type of behavior known as "expanding fixed points".

Our research focuses on the long-term behavior of a non-linear model used for classification, where a stochastic process estimates the impact of input features on hidden variables. This process can be viewed as a variation of a method known as multiple additive regression. The estimator, which approximates this process, uses randomised trees to generate predictions. By applying a specific framework to the analysis, which measures the complexity of data through its dimensions rather than the number of data points, we are able to show that the estimator's predictions follow a normal distribution, even when the underlying data does not. Furthermore, our results imply that the accuracy of the estimator's predictions is directly proportional to the square root of the data's dimensions.

A novel Communication-Restricted-ADMM framework is introduced for managing unbalanced distribution networks with numerous electric vehicle charging stations. This framework effectively addresses communication interdependence issues by limiting inter-subsystem exchanges to a single variable. It achieves this through the utilization of a unified reference point, allowing for the optimization of power distribution within separate regions of the network. Communication requirements are minimized as only a shared variable needs to be exchanged between regions, while local optimization variables remain local. Using the UK's West Midlands as a case study, the proposed framework demonstrates its potential in reducing communication needs by 50% or more compared to traditional multi-subsystem approaches.

To determine the electronic properties and structural features of $SmFeO_3$ in its orthorhombic $Pmm2$ phase, a computational study was conducted. The research examined the structural, elastic, and electronic characteristics of $SmFeO_3$ using density functional theory with the incorporation of the Hubbard U parameter. The findings indicate that the orthorhombic $Pmm2$ phase exhibits stability. The calculated density of states and band structure show that both 3$d$ and 4$d$ states are localized in the valence band, while the conduction band is comprised of these states. The investigation also reveals that $SmFeO_3$ exhibits semiconducting behavior, with the conduction band's top edge being influenced by the $Fe$-$O$ bond.

A comprehensive model for the dynamics of bacterial pathways in a cell culture has been proposed. Key cell processes such as DNA replication, cell division, protein production, and the presence of multiple pathways for cell maintenance are accounted for. The cell culture is modeled as a two-dimensional grid, where spatial factors are considered in cell division and maintenance. Each cell is characterized by its age, having at least one active pathway, and the model demonstrates that cell culture growth follows a logistic curve. Furthermore, the model exhibits a phase transition where the cell culture can either sustainably coexist with its environment or not, depending on the cell division and death rates. These findings are validated using the Wolfram Mathematica platform and are based on empirical data.

Achieving a comfortable indoor environment while minimizing energy consumption is crucial, and proper ventilation systems play a key role in this effort. Conventional fixed ventilation systems are not suitable for achieving flexibility in building ventilation, and fully adaptable ventilation systems, although effective, can be overly expensive and lack a clear understanding of the optimal set points. This paper proposes a data-driven approach to developing a predictive model for an experimental room with an adjustable ventilation system. By using data from sensors and occupancy information, the model can accurately predict the room's conditions and suggest the optimal set points for energy-saving without compromising comfort. This model can be applied to small-sized rooms and may also be used as a foundation for a more comprehensive control strategy that can be easily adapted to other buildings with similar characteristics and similar control systems.

We examined the development of a peculiar type of supernova (SLSNe-I) by combining the outcomes of various observations with computer simulations. The investigation involved analyzing the light output of a supernova called 2017gci, which had different patterns in its early stages. Our analysis suggests that the light output of this event was primarily due to the expansion of a massive, low-velocity cloud of material that was powered by the heat released from nuclear reactions. However, the initial stages of this event were affected by the interaction between this cloud and a surrounding dust cloud, which caused the light output to be uneven. Our models indicate that the expansion of a massive core containing the progenitor star and the surrounding material was likely driven by the heat released from nuclear reactions. The analysis also suggests that the distance to this event was relatively close, which caused the light output of nearby stars to interfere with the measurements. The investigation of this event provides further evidence for the multiple paths that can lead to the creation of SLSNe-I and highlights the need for further research to understand the nature of these events.

The impact of external magnetic fields on two-dimensional materials with a single magnetic domain is investigated. A novel equation of motion is developed to describe the magnetization dynamics within these materials, taking into account a specific type of precession that occurs when the magnetic field is weak. A phenomenological theory is formulated to account for the random orientation of domain walls in single-domain particles, and it is applied to predict the magnetization curve of CoO(0001) single-domain grains under various magnetic field conditions. These predictions were compared with the results of micromagnetic simulations and were found to be in good agreement.

A well-known challenge in question answering is the "one answer to ten questions" problem, where a single answer is linked to multiple questions by dependency relationships. To address this, we've developed an approach that combines visual awareness with linguistic knowledge to generate these dependencies programmatically. This involves determining the visual awareness of a question relative to its corresponding answer, which is then used to identify the type of relationship between them. By analyzing this visual awareness, we can determine the nature of the dependency between the question and answer, thereby establishing a meaningful connection between them. To validate our approach, we've created a new dataset of answer dependencies annotated by crowdsourced workers. Our experiments show that our method outperforms traditional techniques such as BERT-base and BERT-Large.

Most machine learning models rely on input data that is first converted into a numerical or vector format, making feature attribution a crucial step in ensuring model transparency. Despite numerous methods available, there's still no universally accepted feature attribution technique due to the lack of a single, accurate solution. Our objective is to examine and compare the performance of feature attribution methods in various computer vision tasks. A thorough evaluation of feature attribution techniques is conducted using a range of models across image classification, object detection, and semantic segmentation tasks. A key innovation of our study lies in the utilization of a unique set of tasks that involve multi-label images, multi-modal data, and objects with complex shapes. Our results indicate that certain feature attribution methods excel in these tasks, often within specific model types. These findings suggest that no single method is universally effective and highlight the need for more research on feature attribution techniques.

We examine the linear stability of throat-trapped wormholes in higher dimensions, specifically a specific higher-dimensional model of wormholes. This model includes two masses and a wormhole metric that doesn't follow standard symmetry rules. First, we calculate a specific value for this model based on two masses. Next, we look at how this value changes under different conditions. We then investigate how these wormholes behave when subject to small disturbances. The results show a specific range in which wormholes with two visible images form. This range is limited by the stability of the wormholes when subject to small disturbances. We also find that a specific property of the spacetime, related to light rays not crossing the throat, holds true for wormholes that are stable in this range.

We examine the set of all $n!$ permutations within the $n$-dimensional unit cube $[0, 1)^n$, focusing on the set ${\mathcal P}_n$ that remains when we exclude those permutations whose coordinates add up to $1$. The permutations in ${\mathcal P}_n$ are termed 'bad permutations'. A significant aspect of our analysis is determining the 'entropy disparity' $\Delta_{{\mathcal P}_n}$, which represents the difference in Shannon entropy between uniform distributions on ${\mathcal P}_n$ and the set of all $n!$ permutations, denoted by ${\mathcal P}$, normalized by $n!$. Notably, our analysis reveals that $\Delta_{{\mathcal P}_n}$ converges to $\frac{1}{2e}$ as $n$ approaches infinity. Our findings also extend to the study of 'random strides', which involve subsets of the $n$-dimensional unit cube. The key disparity $\Delta_{{\cal S}_n}$ is analogous to $\Delta_{{\cal P}_n}$ and represents the difference in Shannon entropy between uniform distributions on ${\cal S}_n$ and the set of all $n!$ permutations, normalized by $n!$. The disparity $\Delta_{{\cal S}_n}$ converges to $\frac{1}{4e}$ as $n$ approaches infinity. A significant

Recent studies utilizing a trimer shield model have suggested a new superconducting state in certain materials, yet the theoretical basis for this remains unclear. In an attempt to advance understanding, we've proposed a list of questions to motivate further research, focusing on experimental methods and theoretical modeling that could contribute to resolving these mysteries. For example, how do different trimers interact in these materials and what role do other factors like magnetic orards, electron correlations, and electron-phonon interactions play? Furthermore, we've explored the potential for using symmetry-based models to explain observed phenomena using group theory, utilising this approach to reveal unanswered questions and foster progress in this area.

This paper introduces a novel domain adaptation technique that trains two separate machine learning models, one for predicting the target distribution and one for identifying reciprocal data points. The developed classifier, called the Reciprocal Sample Classifier, utilizes a novel loss function to effectively adapt to target domains with limited supervision. The proposed method's efficacy was extensively evaluated on various datasets, resulting in notable improvements over traditional domain adaptation techniques. Specifically, this approach outperformed robust transfer closure methods, achieving accuracy gains of up to 5.9% for regression tasks and up to 12.4% for classification tasks within the MNIST-MNIST scenario, as well as substantial accuracy improvements of up to 11.7% for classification and 7.6% for regression on more complex datasets like CIFAR10-Cifar100 and SVHN-MNIST.

This research introduces a pioneering method for accurately extracting the 3D pose of automobiles from standard two-dimensional images. The approach leverages the benefits of stereo imaging and combines data from multiple sources, including a database of 3D models and a repository of category-specific shapes. The novel technique commences by utilizing a database of 3D models generated through stereo image processing to calculate the orientation of the automobile. Subsequently, it employs a pre-existing database of category-specific shapes to identify the correct automobile model and determine its precise shape alignment. The approach culminates in generating a highly detailed, accurate model of the automobile using a combination of image data and the selected 3D model. Through testing on a database of 3D models and real-world images, the method has demonstrated its ability to achieve accurate results on both synthetic and real-world data at a speed of 16 frames per second.

This study presents an innovative approach to generating query graphs for knowledge graph embeddings, where each node or edge can be supplemented with an optional filling component to retrieve more detailed information. The creation of query graphs is formulated as a process of iteratively selecting nodes and edges, and is treated as a process of filling a sequence with tokens subject to various constraints. To efficiently solve this problem, we developed an algorithm that makes use of efficient constraint checking enabled by knowledge graph embeddings, and further enhance its performance by incorporating a sampling strategy. The effectiveness of our method is demonstrated through experiments on diverse datasets, yielding impressive results.

This paper presents novel algebraic structures defined by sets of polynomial compositions and monoid realms. These realms find practical application in resolving linear systems with multiple variables, and a methodology is developed and demonstrated through an illustrative example.

Accurate understanding of entities and their connections is vital for making informed decisions. Yet, the constantly changing nature of these entities in real-world applications means that new methods for processing complex, streaming data are necessary. In this research, we explore the effectiveness of various named entity resolution techniques on real datasets, comparing the efficiency and accuracy of these methods. We also developed a new, time-based approach that takes into account changes in the transitivity and similarity of entities over time. Our experiments reveal that state-of-the-art techniques are not always the most effective, and even the best methods can be improved upon.

In the presence of new physics beyond the Standard Model, the conventional adjustments to oblique parameters $S$, $T$, and $U$ no longer accurately reflect the contributions of this new physics. The scenario is particularly relevant in the context of the Minimal Supersymmetric Standard Model, which has been constrained by the recent measurements of the $W$-boson mass and the top quark's electroweak width. The contributions to the oblique parameters from the Higgs, scalar neutral Higgs bosons, and other scalar particles like the light and heavy scalar top quarks, are calculated at one-loop level in a simplified model with a single set of mixing between the third generation and the first two and/or third of the third generation's mixings. The calculations reveal that the adjustments to the oblique parameters $S$, $T$, and $U$ are substantial and necessary to match the supersymmetric predictions with the conventional adjustments derived from the Standard Model. The adjustments to the oblique parameters $S$, $T$, and $U$ are significant and necessary to match the supersymmetric predictions with the conventional adjustments derived from the Standard Model.

We present a novel approach that generates perspective views from dynamic video footage captured by a single moving camera. This method enables the creation of 3D dynamic scenes from dynamic 2D input, utilizing a pose-aware model that accurately captures the 3D structure of the scene. Our technique leverages cutting-edge depth estimation and pose estimation techniques, incorporating a novel depth-based refinement module to significantly improve depth estimation from dynamic video. We evaluate our approach using a newly acquired dynamic dataset, Dynamic Kitsap, which comprises 16, 20 and 35 frames per second video sequences captured by a moving camera. We assess the effectiveness of our method using both quantitative metrics, such as 3D error, normal error, and SSIM, and a user study, demonstrating that our method generates highly realistic perspectives from dynamic video footage.

We examine the requirements for the coefficients of rough differential equations with an added non-linear damping term to have a pseudo-dynamical degree of ${\frac{1}{2}}$. This condition is met when the diffusion coefficient is bounded by H\"older continuity and when the drift coefficient is sufficiently small in the sense of Holder regularity, provided that the starting point is within a specific Stratonovich control set.

A random grain model is utilized, where the variable grain size is randomly chosen from a set of distinct values, representing different physical processes occurring at varying scales. Using a martingale technique, the lower bound for the expected value of any nonlinear function of this random system is derived. It is demonstrated that the variance of the system's output bears a direct relationship with the expected value, proportional to the square of the grain size. An application of this method is presented in a numerical study, analyzing the random system in relation to Burgers' equation, with random viscosity parameter $\nu$. An investigation of the random solution's behavior for short and long times reveals the lower bound for the expected value of a nonlinear function of the random grain model, without confirming the expected long-term correlation between the system's initial and final states.

The integration of intelligent, adaptive, and controllable elements in wireless communication systems is poised to revolutionize future networks by utilizing the full potential of the radio wave transmission process. This can be achieved through the implementation of smart surfaces, allowing for the precise control of signals as they pass through or reflect off their constituent materials. With advanced technologies such as metamaterials and phononic crystals, it is now possible to manipulate the phase, magnitude, and polarization of signals in a more flexible and efficient manner. This paper provides an in-depth review of the latest advancements in intelligent surfaces, including their applications, benefits, and limitations, as well as challenges and design requirements for their practical implementation. Furthermore, we present a comprehensive simulation of the potential performance enhancements offered by reconfigurable intelligent surfaces in fifth-generation, LTE, and Wi-Fi networks, demonstrating their ability to significantly improve data transfer rates and efficiency.

The paper's primary contribution is a method to simplify the analysis of complex multi-agent systems exhibiting stable and unstable behavior. By integrating the concepts of dynamical systems and multi-agent systems, this method uses a stability-based partitioning approach to divide the state space into distinct regions. This technique retains essential features of the original system, such as probabilistic transitions and rewards, while providing a simplified representation that preserves the original system's properties. Furthermore, this method is scalable and enables the identification of global equilibrium states within these multi-agent systems.

Deep learning models are becoming increasingly popular for event-driven cameras, but the performance of their neural networks is often limited by the constraints imposed by embedded platforms such as the ASIC-based Event-Cam. Cams like Event-Cam have very limited computational resources, with only 1 TOPS (Tera-Operations per Second) available, meaning complex networks like ResNet50 cannot be processed in real-time. To overcome this, we propose an innovative approach called Cyclic Training of Multiple Quantization Phases (CTMQ), which allows a complex network to be compressed into a smaller size while maintaining performance. CTMQ achieves this through a cycle-consistency loss that enables multiple training phases, each with distinct quantization schemes tailored to the network's layers. By employing an efficient quantization scheme and quantizing the network in an incremental manner, CTMQ ensures that the network's accuracy is not compromised, even when processing an increasing number of parameters. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach by achieving a 55% reduction in model size without sacrificing accuracy, allowing for the processing of 5 TOPS on Event-Cam. Moreover, our approach can be applied to other types of cameras, such as RGB and NPU, and is highly adaptable.

The core-collapse supernova phenomenon is extensively studied, whereas Type Ia supernovae, which stem from white-dwarf mergers, remain relatively understudied despite their significance in cosmological research. We present a novel theoretical framework for white-dwarf mergers, grounded in cutting-edge multi-dimensional simulations of merging double degenerate systems. The outcome of these simulations is a supernova that closely resembles a sub-Chandrasekhar-mass event, characterized by an explosion energy of approximately $2\times10^{51}$ ergs, a nickel-56 yield of roughly $10^{-2} M_\odot$, and a total radioactive decay energy release of roughly $5\times10^{44}$ ergs. The associated optical burst is accompanied by a distinctive early ultraviolet radiation pattern, which gradually shifts to a prolonged, late-time far ultraviolet radiation lasting multiple thousands of days. The resulting spectral curves exhibit notable differences from those of standard Type Ia supernovae, with both spectral shape and luminosity deviating from standard templates. Notably, the early-time spectral shape is characterized by a pronounced far-ultraviolet component, which gradually diminishes over the subsequent months. Theoretical models of these sub-Chandrasekhar-mass events are also presented and compared to actual observations.

In large-scale educational settings, traditional classroom models often fall short in providing personalized learning experiences. With advancements in online education, there are now more opportunities to implement education at a larger scale. One promising approach involves leveraging AI-driven educational tools to deliver customized learning content. Despite the potential, implementing these solutions in real-world settings is challenging due to practical and theoretical concerns. To address these issues, we conducted a case study on designing and deploying a personalized learning system for a massive educational institution in Singapore, which educates over 30,000 students across 100 schools. Our research identified key design and deployment challenges faced by educators in large-scale educational settings, including the complexity of real-world educational scenarios, the need for efficient learning and deployment of AI models, and the integration of AI-powered education into the existing school curriculum.

The COVID-19 pandemic has resulted in the loss of countless lives and a significant decline in the quality of life for those affected. Despite considerable progress in vaccine development and distribution, many countries continue to grapple with vaccine availability issues. In response to these challenges, countries have introduced innovative solutions for prioritizing access to the vaccine, such as providing it to those most in need. In addition, there is a pressing need to develop effective strategies for tracking vaccine administration and verifying immunization status. To this end, we propose an open-source solution that leverages blockchain technology to streamline vaccine registration and monitoring processes. Our solution, which is currently in use by a large public hospital in Singapore, has improved the efficiency of their vaccine registration and monitoring operations.

Recent advancements in educational data analysis have led to several innovative methods, particularly in student performance evaluation and recommendation. One such approach is data clustering, which groups students based on their learning patterns. In this study, we explore the application of clustering techniques to course level. Our primary objective is to identify student learning trends across the entire course spectrum and reveal the underlying structures in their behavior patterns. We also aim to determine which courses benefit most from using these patterns, and whether clustering can facilitate effective resource allocation and improve student outcomes by targeting specific groups.

The Lattice League model is an exactly solvable two-dimensional complex gauge theory that exhibits both particle and antiparticle symmetry and localization properties. This symmetry is associated with a parameter $\kappa$, which, when not equal to one, leads to a breakdown of these symmetries. This breakdown results in the emergence of a gapped ground state, characterized by non-zero Chern-Simons levels for both particles and antiparticles on a torus. This effect is strongest on a torus and weakest on a sphere. This paper utilizes a loop expansion framework to study this phenomenon, using a method to break down the loop field theory into a series of integrals involving Chern-Simons levels. This approach allows for a detailed understanding of how the loop expansion relates to the breakdown of particle-antiparticle symmetry in the model, ultimately revealing a connection to a series expansion of the gapped ground state's non-commutative torus geometry.

A new type of collective movement among strongly magnetized electrons in a two-dimensional layer is discovered, where a specific movement mode with angular momentum is significantly slowed down due to the interaction between electron spins and the magnetic field. This mode, however, remains unaffected by the interaction between electron movements and the magnetic field. The identified mode could be useful in studying the interaction between electron spins and the magnetic field.

We've discovered that the dynamics of the driven Ising chain can be exactly solved in the conformal field theory limit through a simple analytical approach, which is valid even when the driving frequency deviates from the golden ratio, $\frac{\sqrt{5}-1}{2}$. This allows us to examine the behavior of the model under nearby protocols, with our results indicating that both the quantum spectral form and the entanglement entropy are well-approximated by those seen in the conformal field theory at low frequencies. However, a significant anomaly arises in the entanglement entropy at finite frequencies, which is attributed to the finite size effect, as well as the non-conformal structure of the Floquet spectrum. We've also found that the entanglement entropy exhibits periodic fluctuations in the vicinity of the golden ratio frequency, which can be attributed to the emergence of a hidden conformal symmetry at this driving frequency. Our work provides a comprehensive understanding of the conformal field theory in 1+1 dimensions, which is applicable to driven Ising chain protocols and predicts the existence of a conformal anomaly near the golden ratio frequency.

Our innovative fusion model is designed to process multiple sensor types by
extracting and combining data from fusion sensors and multimodal sensors within a
neural network. This allows for enhanced learning and error correction in the
latent space, resulting in improved tracking performance. To evaluate the model's
effectiveness, we conducted experiments utilizing the racing car dataset, and
the findings demonstrate its potential as a sophisticated fusion system.

We have made two significant measurements at the LHCb experiment using $pp$
collisions recorded at a centre-of-mass energy of 8 TeV with an integrated
luminosity of 3 fb$^{-1}$. The first result is the $B_s$ mixing phase, which we
determined to be $0.21^{+0.14}_{-0.10}(stat.) \pm0.06(syst.)$ radians, agreeing
with the current Standard Model prediction. The second result is the CP-violating
phase associated with the decay of $B_s$ to three pions, determined to be $-0.014^{+0.005}_{-0.003}(stat.)\pm 0.010 (syst.)$ radians, leading to a CP-violation estimate of approximately $-0.0004^{+0.0010}_{-0.0014}(stat.)\pm 0.0011 (syst.)$.

This research investigates infinite-time optimal control problems across closed-form and infinite-dimensional linear quadratic problems with discrete-time and continuous-time systems. These problems involve state and control constraints, with a focus on distributed ideal control. This control strategy requires information from all network nodes and yields fully decentralized control laws. Key findings involve the development of necessary and sufficient conditions for the existence of distributed ideal controllers, the examination of the continuous-time infinite dimensional control problem, and the derivation of a practical algorithm for the synthesis of decentralized controllers for network systems. These results are supported by numerical examples.

In labeled random finite set (LRFS) tracking, detecting new targets and resolving birth-death uncertainty is crucial, particularly when multiple sensors exhibit combined birth rates for newly detected targets. A novel multi-sensor adaptive birth sampler (MS-Abs) is introduced to achieve this. This proposed approach enhances sample generation from the birth process by taking into account combined sensor measurements that exhibit varying birth rates. A two-sensor scenario is initially examined, followed by an extension to N-sensor cases, yielding more efficient and targeted birth rates. MS-Abs is applied within a labeled random finite set framework that incorporates a global color multi-Bernoulli model for managing existing targets and absorbing birth samples. This method is evaluated through simulation studies demonstrating its effectiveness in combination with other target models and data association techniques.

Linguists have been collecting language attributes for over a century, with the latest update to the World Atlas of Language Structures adding over 1,000 properties for 848 languages. This collaborative project presents a unique challenge: predicting attributes using machine learning and language data. By providing a set of 42 attributes, the participants were tasked with developing models that could forecast their presence or absence for over 1,000 languages, with the goal of identifying missing information for languages with incomplete profiles. This report presents the participating teams' approaches, their results, and the winners of the shared task.

Reinforcement learning algorithms have seen significant success across a variety of fields.  However, their application in real-world settings is hindered by the need for feedback from the environment.  This limitation necessitates the use of off-policy evaluation, a technique that allows users to determine how well an existing policy might perform.  This article provides an in-depth review of off-policy evaluation techniques, analyzing both constraint-free and constrained methods before discussing open issues and proposing potential research directions.

Developing biotechnology drugs is notoriously challenging. To improve this process, understanding the historical failure rates of similar collections can be beneficial. However, gathering this information is often costly and time-consuming, and gathering it may not be necessary in all cases. Our research focuses on determining the optimal point to initiate collecting failure data, balancing the costs of collecting data with potential project savings. To achieve this, we model the decision as a sequential comparison of expected profits based on data that is being sampled. By applying this approach, we can identify the optimal decision-making strategy, and demonstrate that this strategy can be represented as a value function tied to a supervisor's state, which can be determined through backward induction. To implement this approach, we propose a value iteration algorithm that can be used to identify the optimal decision-making strategy. Additionally, we explore the value of incorporating multiple failure datasets into a single decision-making problem, and demonstrate that this can lead to more consistent decisions. To achieve this, we can combine the historical failure data using a weighted average, and demonstrate that this results in a Bayesian network with a specific structure.

In this paper, we investigate the relationship between energy and momentum for a polaron within the context of the multi-polaronic Hubard model. Our analysis focuses on the ground state of a finite system in one-dimensional space as the system size approaches infinity. While the k-particle energy relation is bounded above by a finite value, E approximately less than or equal to k^2/a_0, for large k values, the polynomial bound is exact for small k values. However, the remaining error range decreases exponentially with system size and is dominated by the ground state correlation function, exhibiting exponential decay.

We investigate the long-term stability of operators in holographic plasma subject to a constant external electromagnetic force, which we model using an electrodynamic boundary condition. Simulations reveal that operators with large quantum numbers become exponentially unstable and eventually disappear over time, while those with small quantum numbers experience gradual loss due to a power-law decay. Notably, the decay exponent is influenced by the magnetic field strength and the frequency of the applied force, which also determines the boundary condition. In the context of the holographic correspondence, this instability implies a continuous energy influx from the AdS 'bath' to the boundary to compensate for energy losses.

Our approach involves proving that within a specific framework, certain quantum systems exhibiting the Heisenberg complementarity principle must be represented by a tomographic model that is generically two-design. This result naturally leads to a geometric interpretation, demonstrating the existence of feline states, which are states that, when quantized, give rise to Schr\"odingen feline optics - a subset of quantum optics where the wave function of a quantum state is constrained to lie on a unit hyperboloid. Importantly, these feline states are constrained to exhibit unit hyperboloid evolution, mirroring Schr\"odingen feline optics. Additionally, by assuming the existence of feline states, we are able to derive the universality of two-designs for generically bi-Designable states.

The cyclic decomposition theorem, first introduced by Plante, demonstrates that any orientation-preserving diffeomorphism of a compact manifold has a cyclic decomposition. This implies the existence of a cyclic sequence of points ${\bf Q}$ and a corresponding sequence of points ${\bf P}$, all located on the manifold, such that each point in ${\bf P}$ is close to a close return of a point in ${\bf Q}$. This theorem has various applications, including a condition for when the average derivative of an orientation-preserving diffeomorphism equals one. Furthermore, a nonexpansive curve on a compact surface cannot be orientation-preserving.

This article outlines a novel method for determining the Gromov-Hausdorff distance between metric spaces $X$ and $Y$, involving the utilization of the Borsuk problem and Borsuk quantity. This approach enables the establishment of the Gromov-Hausdorff lower bound for $d_{GH}(X,Y)$ and provides a method to identify when $d_{GH}(X,Y)=0$. Additionally, we demonstrate that the introduced algorithm offers superior asymptotic complexity over existing methods for one specific instance. Moreover, the algorithm's potential to be integrated with other techniques for calculating Gromov-Hausdorff distance is discussed.

This work focuses on homogenization, specifically the fourth-order tensors with wavy patterns that describe elastic materials with periodic inclusions. By developing new methods, we can more accurately estimate the elastic properties of materials with small-scale inclusions. Traditional methods, however, lose accuracy as the scale of these inclusions gets very small. By instead analyzing a high-frequency behavior in tensors with periodic structures, we can improve estimates and identify key factors contributing to elastic properties at a homogenized level. This approach leads to simplified formulas for certain tensors, while for others, they become a combination of a 'homogenized' matrix and a matrix that decreases in magnitude as the scale of inclusion gets very small. Moreover, we can further refine these formulas by increasing the order of the approximation.

Recent advancements in task-driven dialogue systems have led to the development of a new generation of multilingual chatbots capable of handling various tasks across different devices. To enhance the performance of these systems in diverse environments, it is essential to consider the impact of different domains, languages, and frameworks on their effectiveness. This research investigates the impact of different conversational frameworks on task-driven dialogue systems by comparing the performance of five distinct architectures, including BERT, GPT, GPT-2, Transformer, and RoBERTa, in various languages and domains. The results indicate that RoBERTa emerges as a highly competitive model that outperforms its peers in different languages and domains, especially in tasks that involve reading and answering complex questions.

This paper presents an interface in C++ that allows for interactions with SMT solvers, enabling a script-driven access independent of specific solver libraries. The interface consists of templates for assertions and queries, along with a method to generate certificates, a timer for solving operations, and a unique ID for managing models. The evaluation demonstrates the interface's versatility across various SMT solvers, and a Python script is provided illustrating its use.

A novel method is proposed to construct quasi-exactly solvable systems by applying a transformation to exactly soluble potential systems. This approach involves transforming the eigenstates of a well-known exactly soluble potential through a non-local transformation. To test the validity of the newly constructed quasicellular potential, an analytical expression for the partition function is derived and used to calculate the higher moments of the eigenvalue distribution. This distribution is found to be consistent with the predicted behavior of the Tracy-Widom distribution under certain conditions, such as in the case of the anharmonic oscillator potential transformed by the Bender-Dunne variable. This suggests that the quasicellular potential may be a viable model for understanding complex systems.

Deep learning models have become the preferred choice for classifying physical signals, particularly due to the abundance of readily available datasets. However, these models face a significant limitation: they struggle to perform well when given low-quality data. To address this issue, we developed a straightforward yet effective technique to enhance the clarity of sensor data, thus improving the accuracy of machine learning models even when there's no increase in parameters or computational cost (FLOPS).

The DART mission's impact on Dimorphos is expected to increase the asteroid's rotation energy, potentially causing material to shift from its secondary component to the primary one. This phenomenon may be similar to the effect observed in the Scheila asteroid, whose shape change is thought to result from the asteroid's own rotation causing loose material to break off. This shape change is thought to have occurred due to the asteroid's secondary component colliding with and ejecting material from the primary one. The collision's efficiency is expected to depend heavily on the relative rotation rate of the secondary component. Given that Dimorphos' rotation speed is thought to be roughly 0.1 second of a day, it is plausible that the asteroid's secondary component could collide with and eject material from the primary one.

We investigate the interaction of scalar charged fields with a Reissner-Nordstrom black hole, focusing on the bound state spectrum and the scalar field's behavior at the black hole horizon. We specifically examine two types of scalar charged formations: a Gaussian shell and a charged spherical shell with constant charge density. We calculate the effective potential and identify its local features, determine the bound state spectrum, and compute the mass and charge of the black hole. We show that for a Gaussian shell, the black hole retains its physical properties under arbitrary coupling, resulting in hair-free solutions. We also explore the effects of varying the shell's parameters and the gravitational constant on the bound state spectrum. Furthermore, we analyze the behavior of the scalar field and the energy-momentum tensor inside the shell, and demonstrate that it is possible to create a scalar charged formation around the black hole without altering its physical properties.

The possibility of active-sterile neutrinos mixing at low energies has been proposed to resolve issues with some anomalies in the MiniBooNE and MiniBooNE experiments. This paper examines the scenario where a sterile neutrino coexists at GeV energies with a nearly zero-mass state separated by a very small mass difference. An upper limit for the active-sterile mixing parameter is derived based on existing data, and the potential for future experiments to detect evidence of an additional low-energy state is explored. The analysis reveals that even with low energy resolution, it may still be feasible to observe a low-energy peak in the sterile neutrino energy spectrum, especially if the sterile neutrino's mass is below 100 MeV. The proposed experiments would either confirm this scenario or set more stringent constraints on the sterile neutrino's parameters.

The goal of self-supervised picture denoising is to remove noise from images without explicit guidance. A novel Cyclic multi-Variate Function for Self-supervised Picture denoising, referred to as CVF-SID, has been developed to accomplish this. The CVF-SID framework consists of three distinct phases: Firstly, the input image is processed through a series of multi-variate functions and its various feature maps are generated at different scales. Secondly, the framework utilizes an unsupervised discriminator network to differentiate the features derived from the input image and those obtained from a noisy image. Lastly, the input image is reconstructed by combining the various feature maps, resulting in a more accurate and detailed image restoration. Experimental results demonstrate that CVF-SID outperforms leading self-supervised denoising methods, including DNN, and is on par with the current state-of-the-art deep denoising network, DNN + DSN, on benchmark datasets, including synthetic and real-world images.

The objective of the $\ell_0$ or Bernstein-Thomae problem is to reconstruct a sparse signal from randomly selected linear measurements, where the signal is composed of real values from the set {0,1}. This problem is challenging due to the vast number of possible functions for the inverse linear transformation. We have devised an algorithm that can identify the correct reconstruction intention when a sufficient number of measurements are taken, where the number of required measurements is determined by the signal's dimension and the expected number of active components. This algorithm achieves this by applying a probabilistic method to construct a suitable basis for the sparse signal space. Furthermore, our algorithm yields a better outcome when the signal has fewer active components than the expected number, where the signal's dimension and the number of active components determine the number of required measurements. This problem is also explored in the context of machine learning and compressive sensing, where the results demonstrate the feasibility of the proposed method.

Real-world problems frequently necessitate tackling multiple objectives simultaneously, which can be characterized as set unions or intersections. This paper investigates the agreement problem for unions and intersections of various sets. The agreement problem seeks to identify whether at least one element from a collection of sets satisfies a particular condition by being a member of that set. For sets of cardinality $k$, the agreement problem can be solved in $O(k \cdot 2^{O(k \log \log k)}}$ time using a randomized algorithm, while a deterministic algorithm requires $O(m + k \cdot 2^{O(k \log \log k)}}$ time. Notably, even when dealing with sets of a constant number of sets, the known algorithms' running times significantly outperform their practical counterparts, which often rely on naive approaches with much larger running times, typically proportional to $O(mk)$.

A crucial issue in reinforcement learning is efficient motor learning for complex tasks. We propose a new method called end-effect investigation, which involves generating multiple initial policies and using them to collect data from a goal-free environment. This data is used to create an optimal policy, which performs better than policies derived from single trajectory data. We show that this method can be efficient when the final goal can be easily defined. We also found that using multiple policies can be more efficient than exploring different policies in a goal-free, random setting.

A common approach for analyzing a system's thermal characteristics involves calculating its capacity, which is a derivative of its Boltzmann factor. For complex systems, this can be done by determining the system's partition function under specific conditions and then deriving the characteristic function. In the context of a Brownian particle confined by a nonlinear potential, which is often used as a model for observing anomalies in thermal behavior, the required partition function has been derived for a particular scenario. By utilizing this partition function, we demonstrate that the renormalized frequency, which is a renormalized quantity derived from the propagator, can be directly converted into a system's thermal characteristics.

We have carried out a detailed numerical investigation into the two-point correlations of conformally invariant theories that operate on a two-dimensional plane with a slit cut. This slit has either one or two holes depending on the type of geometric structure known as a "Dirichlet domain". Our analysis focused on the behavior of these correlations when the two points are very close to each other and the data was obtained by averaging over random domain geometries. This led us to discover that for points very close to each other the correlations follow a specific pattern that can be described using a combination of two Gaussian functions, one of which has a large standard deviation and the other one has a standard deviation that is inversely proportional to the length of the cut. This specific behavior is a result of a specific type of geometric feature known as a "crosscap" and it is a direct result of a mathematical formula that describes the behavior of these correlations when the domain geometry is idealized.

Twitter suspended Niche Gateway, a company that generated automated tweets for clients, following allegations of its role in spreading misinformation associated with the 2020 U.S. presidential election. Although the decision to ban Niche Gateway has contributed to a decline in automated account activity, little is known about the company's operations pre-ban. This research delves into Niche Gateway's pre-ban Twitter account, analyzing its behavior and connections to similar accounts. A manual investigation of 1,000 accounts revealed their intricate connections and confirmed the existence of shared account patterns. Furthermore, the study proposes a method to identify accounts linked to Niche Gateway based on their behavior and content, enabling the detection of similar accounts existing on Twitter.

This paper's objective is to provide a comprehensive theoretical review of the LHC's operating conditions. It commences with an examination of the LHC's general characteristics, followed by a detailed explanation of the principles underlying strong interactions. Subsequently, the model employed to investigate the behavior of strong interactions is discussed in depth. Additionally, the report covers the key concepts of the standard model, along with an exhaustive analysis of the LHC's experimental results.

Crowdsourced evaluation methods, such as crowdsourcing, can be beneficial for identifying the quality of image classification models, but are often marred by inaccuracies and inconsistencies. This leads to unclear and unreliable results. To address these issues, a new post-processing technique is proposed that involves combining multiple models to create an ensemble, using crowdsourced data uncertainty as a guide. This method leverages crowd signals to create a 'human softmax' vector representing the collective opinions of the crowd and employs it to weight the individual models' uncertainty estimates with a relevance metric. This metric is calculated by comparing the 'human softmax' vector to the softvoting prediction of the respective model and then normalized. This approach enables the selection of the most relevant data points and reduces the impact of noisy ones. Evaluations on the crowd-sourced datasets, CUB and ImageNet, demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed technique in producing more reliable performance estimates and achieving better model rankings compared to traditional methods, such as inter-rater reliability.

In the context of the 5G cellular network, vehicle-to-everything communication is characterized by various associated networks and shifting vehicle-to-BS connections. To address this issue, our research presents a novel reinforcement learning method that enables vehicles to concurrently maintain connections with multiple BSs and distribute information adaptively across different networks. The primary objective is to maximize the overall data transmission rate by balancing the average network traffic and individual vehicle throughput. To achieve this, the system is formulated as a multi-agent reinforcement learning problem, where vehicles learn local policies through the Q-learning algorithm. To improve the convergence rate, we propose a new Q-learning algorithm that incorporates the target value with a gradient-based update rule. Furthermore, our approach incorporates the multi-agent deep Q-network structure, where multiple vehicles share experience and learn in unicast and multicast modes. The effectiveness of our approach is demonstrated through simulations, showing that it achieves higher average network traffic and better average individual throughput compared to existing solutions.

A decade ago, the high-performance computing community prioritized the ImageNet challenge as a benchmark for measuring algorithmic advancements in artificial intelligence. This study marks the tenth anniversary of the challenge, offering a comprehensive examination of advancements in computer vision over the past decade. The findings reveal that deep learning has become the dominant force in computer vision, resulting in the creation of substantial datasets and extensive software collections for computer vision research. The current computer vision landscape, although featuring cutting-edge technologies like edge AI, deep learning frameworks, and specialized hardware, also confronts pressing challenges associated with data quality, model reliability, and environmental sustainability. The study concludes by highlighting the potential of the next decade in artificial intelligence, emphasizing the need for continued innovation and responsible AI practices that prioritize both technical progress and social responsibility.

Feature tickets are typically accompanied by feature toggles, which allow the temporary disable of newly added features, making it easier to integrate them into the main codebase even during ongoing development.

However, feature tickets are often merged into the primary codebase at different times, potentially disrupting other ongoing developments. 

In an effort to gauge the typical usage of feature toggles, researchers analyzed data from 1,500 high-quality open-source projects on GitHub, focusing on how feature tickets are merged into the primary codebase.

The findings indicate that projects frequently utilize feature toggles, especially when initially integrating new features, but often stop doing so before these tickets are resolved. 

Moreover, projects that frequently employ feature toggles are less likely to experience issues related to these toggles, such as merged tickets causing problems or being incorrectly merged together.

The research suggests that feature tickets are often merged into the primary codebase too early, potentially causing issues that could be minimized through more strategic integration strategies.

The Euler equations for incompressible fluids, governed by ideal Navier-Stokes dynamics, exhibit a range of complex behavior across different spatial and temporal scales. This complexity is characterized by singularities that develop on a fractal curve within the fluid's phase space, a concept introduced by Craik and Kleiser. Our study seeks to establish a fundamental bound on the fractal dimension of this curve, with the goal of quantifying the underlying complexity. To achieve this, we employ a rigorous mathematical approach, leveraging certain fundamental principles of the Euler equations and a specific measure of fluid vorticity. Our analysis reveals that this complex behavior is inherent and unavoidable, with the fractal dimension of the curve remaining constant under various conditions. Our results have significant implications, particularly regarding the efficacy of energy-based bounds in predicting fluid vorticity.

In the realm of scientific research, datasets can be classified into two general types: qualitative, which pertain to individual items, and quantitative, which involve measurements. This distinction is also applicable to point clouds, which can contain geometric information about various items. These datasets can then be analyzed using different methods, including shape analysis, which assesses the global characteristics of individual items, and shape comparison, which compares the characteristics of multiple items. The advent of deep learning techniques has significantly enhanced the capabilities of shape analysis, but quantitative analysis of extensive point clouds in scientific research remains a relatively unexplored area. This paper presents a comprehensive case study on categorizing and measuring cuneiform characters using deep learning, which demonstrates the potential for large-scale scientific research using point clouds. The proposed framework utilizes a multi-level approach, which includes a categorization module and a character recognition module. The categorization module identifies the type of cuneiform character, while the character recognition module measures its shape features. The framework's effectiveness is evaluated using a comprehensive dataset of 1,200 comprehensive cuneiform characters, which includes 600 oblong, 400 triangular, and 200 square-shaped characters. The proposed framework successfully achieved an accuracy rate of 99.5% in categorizing the characters and an accuracy rate of 99.0% in shape recognition.

The recent measurement of the muon's anomalous magnetic moment at Fermilab's g-2 experiment revealed a significant discrepancy from the Standard Model's prediction. Several models that could account for this anomaly introduce a spin-2 massive particle, known as the massive spin-2 particle (MS2P), through the tree-level interaction. However, the MS2P's coupling to the muon and photon must be very large to address the anomaly, posing concerns for unitarity and potentially leading to instability in the MS2P's vacuum. Our study focuses on the unitarity constraints for the MS2P in the lowest-order effective field theory, particularly in the transverse MS2P representation. We find that the unitarity limits for the MS2P's coupling, when applied to the muon's g-2 anomaly, are more stringent than those derived from the proton's deep-inelastic scattering measurements for certain values of the MS2P's mass. These constraints may be relaxed if the MS2P's internal structure is taken into account in the effective field theory, allowing for a more accurate assessment of the MS2P's unitarity constraints.

We examine how a hostage-taker's decision is impacted by the presence of hostages and their personal connection to the negotiator, under the assumption that the negotiator can offer a mutually beneficial settlement in exchange for the release of the hostage. The result is a more complex negotiation process that takes into account the negotiator's influence over the hostage-taker, who is motivated by a desire for revenge as well as a willingness to accept a settlement. When the negotiator has a strong relationship with the hostage-taker, they can offer more attractive settlement options, but these have a limited effect. Conversely, when the negotiator has a weak relationship, the hostage-taker is more likely to accept a settlement rather than seek revenge. However, if the hostage-taker is not connected to the negotiator, the hostage-taker seeks revenge even if the negotator offers a favorable settlement. This model can be applied to real-world situations such as a hostage situation or a terrorist attack.

Research reveals a complex relationship between a word's meaning and the grammatical context required for proper interpretation. A study published in 2018 utilized a word's neural representation to examine this interaction, discovering that focusing on a word's role within a sentence context influences the way meaning is interpreted, particularly by modulating both semantic and syntactic information. This work now expands on previous findings by examining the neural representation of thematic roles using a language with complex grammatical structures. By comparing neural representations of disambiguated and ambiguous words, the study found that the context of the sentence plays a significant role in distinguishing between different meanings of a word. Additionally, the study found that neural representations of thematic roles are more accurate and reliable when using a specific type of neural network, and that the neural signals associated with these roles are located in distinct brain regions. These findings suggest that neural representations of thematic roles are processed in a highly specialized and complex manner.

The ANTARES neutrino telescope has implemented a system to notify observers of potential astrophysical transient events through the Gamma-Ray Observatory Trigger and Alert Generation (GTRAG) network. GTRAG's outcomes are disseminated to a network of 0.5 to 2.5 m telescopes in near real-time, allowing experts to verify and analyze the origins of neutrinos and gamma rays. A review of the data collected between 2015 and 2019 revealed 122 positron events, 30 muon-like events, 1 neutrino-like event, and 1 high-energy electron-like event. The causes of these events were examined and discussed, with the aim of distinguishing between astrophysical and background sources.

A recent study has demonstrated that a mirror reflection stage can be effectively integrated into a high-contrast adaptive optics system to optimize its performance. Adaptive optics systems utilize reflection stages to adjust the path of an incoming beam, influencing the focal ratio and, by extension, the instrument's performance. Within a high-contrast adaptive optics setup, this feature can be employed to fine-tune the instrument's performance, accounting for residual aberrations. Research has shown that a mirror reflection stage can be implemented in such systems, and its effectiveness has been validated through experiments. Furthermore, the investigation revealed that the instrument's performance, including its ability to correct aberrations and maintain a high contrast, remains stable even with varying mirror stage settings. With this feature, it's possible to achieve a high contrast level of approximately 4.5 x 10^-6 across the 0.5 to 0.6 wavelength range under the same total light flux.

Lattice dynamics calculations, particularly phonon calculations, are crucial for accurately describing materials and processes, but traditional approaches are often hindered by computational complexity issues. To overcome this, we have developed a hybrid density functional, dubbed ePBE, which is an enhanced version of the widely used PBE functional. This functional, which is based on an empirical ePBE-SIC approach, effectively reduces computational complexity while maintaining reliability, as evidenced by its accurate predictions for a variety of materials. The use of ePBE-SIA has also allowed us to examine the lattice dynamics of small clusters, providing a deeper understanding of the anharmonic effects that occur within them. The results from these calculations demonstrate the potential of ePBE-SIA in simulating the dynamic behavior of materials, with applications in both condensed and gas-phase environments.

In the context of WSTS, specifically Karp-Miller forests with nice metrics under monotone partial orders, this research demonstrates that determining whether a state has a predecessor has a non-elementary complexity. Furthermore, it highlights that generating all the immediate predecessors of a state is feasible in exponential time, $2^{O(n)}$ for KM-forests. Moreover, it establishes that if the transition function's computation is restricted to a single step, then the computational complexity of generating all the immediate predecessors of a state becomes $n^{F}$, where $F$ is a function that increases polynomially with the size of the forest. This paper also outlines the practical implications of these findings, especially in the context of planning, which involves finding a sequence of transitions that transform the initial state into a target state within a specific WSTS.

The 4th Year of the Machine Intelligence Workshop series was held at the RAS on March 9-10, with the event gathering experts from various fields to address challenges and discover novel applications for machine learning. This workshop aimed to explore innovative methods for advancing astronomical research, identifying opportunities, and addressing pressing challenges. This contribution focuses on applying machine learning techniques to the Fermi-LAT 14-year pass data, enabling the generation of a machine-optimized all-sky map and the identification of variable sources.

In a quantum universe governed by an all-encompassing law, traditional notions and their underlying assumptions are put to the test. We examine how the principles of wave function collapse and the measurement problem affect our comprehension of macroscopic objects. We argue that the emergence of the classical realm within the quantum universe cannot be attributed to the act of measurement, as this would necessitate an observer capable of perceiving multiple states, a capacity that defies the emergence of classical states. Instead, we propose an alternative explanation for the emergence of classicality, suggesting it arises from the inherent properties and relationships within the quantum universe. We investigate this idea further by analyzing the properties of entangled systems and developing a framework to explain the emergence of classicality. We demonstrate that the traditional view of objects is an illusion resulting from a lack of knowledge about the quantum universe, comparable to how the universe appears non-disorderly to us despite its constituent particles being probabilistically distributed.

The geometric total of an ellipsoid in n-dimensional space is defined as the product of the lengths of its main axes raised to the powers 4/5, 4/5, and 1. Building upon previous work, we establish a more comprehensive set of exterior constraints for this total when the axes are subject to small perturbations in R^n, encompassing scenarios involving both positive and negative fluctuations.

Tabular data is widely used in various fields like economics, social sciences, and medicine. A novel machine learning method called "Saint" addresses the issue of limited labeled data in tabular models. It leverages row-specific attention to create focused representations, which significantly boost the performance of simple models like logistic regression and more complex ones like deep neural networks. By using contrastive learning during a pre-training phase, Saint establishes a connection between the rows and achieves better results compared to existing methods such as Gradient Boosting and Random Forest. When applied to real-world datasets, Saint's results show state-of-the-art performance in tasks such as student exam prediction and with minimal labeled data required. Its code has been made available for community use at https://github.com/lpiao24/saint.

As deep learning demands increasingly more computational resources, the need to address power consumption, and reduce the size and weight of the systems becomes increasingly pressing. To address these challenges, researchers are exploring the use of transfer learning on embedded devices. This work investigates how the architecture of deep learning models affects their ability to transfer knowledge to new tasks. We examine the impact of model size on the performance of smaller models compared to larger ones on image classification tasks. Our experiments use synthetic data to eliminate variations caused by model training, and reveal that smaller models can achieve similar results to their larger counterparts. We also test the models on real-world datasets to confirm our findings. Our research indicates that model size is not the primary factor influencing performance in these scenarios.

The center-vortex model's potential for resolving the Gribov problem is investigated within the framework of Landau gauge, with a focus on the definition of region $F$ in the Landau gauge as a solution. In this definition, $F$ is comprised of $A_\mu(x)$'s support, with a specified constraint requiring the covariant derivative of a gluon field within this region to be zero. Notably, this definition is capable of resolving the Gribov problem without necessitating additional independent boundary conditions for local Gribov copies, with core regions serving as the key to this resolution.

The detection of dark matter surrounding external galaxies through microlensing has sparked debate about the nature of dark matter and potential sources.  We investigate how the properties of dark matter surrounding large-scale dwarf galaxies can reveal information about dark matter substructure formation.  Analyzing the properties of dark matter within the Large Scale Dwarf Galaxy sample from the Dark Energy Survey, we find that the distribution of dark matter within these galaxies is not significantly affected by the presence of small dark matter substructures.  This result suggests that the formation of large-scale dwarf galaxies is not heavily influenced by nearby substructures.  We also consider the implications of this finding on the possible lifetime of dark matter substructures.

Our goal is to enhance the quality of open knowledge graphs by incorporating
meaningful relationships not yet represented within the graph's structure. To achieve
this, we propose a two-stage approach for discovering new open knowledge graph
concepts. Initially, we develop a method for automatically formulating supplementary
queries to complement the initial open knowledge graph query, aimed at capturing
missing information. Subsequently, we utilize the gathered query results to identify
new open knowledge graph edge candidates, which are then presented to a community
ofvolunteers for validation. Through a comprehensive evaluation involving 12 diverse
datasets, our method demonstrates its effectiveness in discovering up to 236.8% more
new open knowledge graph edges compared to a previous method, even when utilizing the
same initial queries.

We're focusing on linear systems arising from generalized saddle-point techniques used for solving multi-compartment fluid flow in porous media, specifically in a discrete-discontinuous space where fluid flow and pressure vary across different fluid zones. Our objective is to develop parameter-resilient preconditioners for such systems when there are significant changes in the number of fluid zones between the problem formulation and its numerical solution. Inspired by the geometric algebra of vectorial and tensorial products, we propose a non-invertible operator representing the right-hand side matrix, allowing us to formulate a preconditioner using tensor-product-based block-diagonal matrices. Furthermore, we show that the preconditioned system remains stable under ill-conditioned transformations and parameter changes. Numerical simulations have demonstrated the efficiency of this preconditioning method in achieving a relative error of $O(1/R)$ in the residual, independent of the number of fluid zones.

Generating concise and coherent summaries of dialogue is a complex task, especially when dealing with unstructured and informal dialogue formats. Current approaches to this problem primarily focus on extracting key points from conversations without fully considering the relationships between sentences. We propose a novel zero-shot abstractive dialogue summarization approach, the DialogueCC, that leverages a discourse-based model to identify and organize sentence relationships before generating summaries, utilizing pre-trained language models to produce the summaries. Evaluations on the Ubuntu and Ubuntu-OpenSubtitles datasets reveal that the proposed model surpasses baseline models, including GPT-2, in generating summaries that are more accurate, coherent, and robust against sentence rearrangement.

A physically informed deep neural network (DNN) is used to predict the widening of radiofrequency interference cross-sections due to Doppler effect reception at receiver sites. The model is trained on data from an electromagnetic simulator covering various antenna and receiver configurations, frequencies, and the Doppler parameter.
